paraphrase: The knower of brahman attains the highest. On this a verse: brahman is truth, knowledge, the infinite (satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ brahma); whoever knows it hidden in the cave, in the highest space, enjoys all desires together with brahman, the wise. From this self (ātman) space arose; from space wind; from wind fire; from fire water; from water earth; from earth plants; from plants food; from food the person (puruṣa). This person is made of the essence of food (annarasamaya); this is its head, this its right wing, this its left wing, this its self (ātman), this its tail, its support (pratiṣṭhā).
speaker: the Upaniṣad (teaching of the Brahmānandavallī)
notes: The head, wings, self and tail-support are indicated with demonstratives (this, this); the text does not name the parts of the body, and identifying them is not stated in the passage. The Upaniṣad calls each of these an inner self (ātman) "made of" (-maya) something; the word kośa (sheath) is not in this text and belongs to later usage.
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

paraphrase: Verse: he becomes non-being (asat) himself, if he knows brahman as non-being; if one knows "brahman is", then they know him as being (sat). Then the further questions (anupraśnāḥ): does anyone who does not know go to that world after death, or does any knower, departing, attain it? He (the Self) desired: "may I be many, may I be born"; he performed tapas; having performed tapas, he created all this, whatever there is; having created it, he entered into it; having entered it, he became the manifest (sat) and the beyond (tyat), the defined and the undefined, the based and the unbased, understanding and non-understanding, truth and untruth; he became truth. Whatever this is, they call it truth. On this there is a verse.
speaker: the Upaniṣad
notes: The segment opens with the verse (śloka) that closes the preceding anuvāka and then gives the body of the next anuvāka; ref follows the prepared segmentation. paraphrase: In the beginning this was non-being (asat); from it being (sat) was born; it made itself by itself; therefore it is called "well-made" (sukṛta). What is well-made is the essence (rasa); having obtained the essence one becomes blissful. Who would breathe, who would live, if this space (ākāśa) were not bliss (ānanda)? It is this that gives bliss. When one finds fearless support in this — the invisible, the incorporeal (or: selfless), the unexpressed, the unsupported — then he has gone to fearlessness. When one makes even a small gap in it, fear arises for him; that same fear is for the knower who does not reflect (amanvāna). On this there is a verse.
speaker: the Upaniṣad

paraphrase: The Bhṛguvallī (3.1.1-3.10.6): Bhṛgu asks his father Varuṇa for brahman and is told to seek that from which beings are born, live and into which they enter, by tapas (3.1); he knows in turn food, breath, mind, understanding and bliss as brahman, returning each time to be told to seek by tapas (3.2-3.6); the vows about food and the pairs of food and eater (3.7-3.10.1); the upāsanā ascriptions with their fruits (3.10.2-3.10.4); and the knower's passage through the five selves and the chant (3.10.5-3.10.6).
